verified.paper_version: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-13; no later arXiv version was present during this verification
verified.dataset_scope: Six cloud-service categories, 9 production Skills, 98 skill-reference files; production escalated-ticket data are confidential and not released.
verified.evaluation_split: Within each Skill, tickets are chronologically split into four equal parts. The first three are development data and drive simulation, attribution, revision, early stopping and version selection. The fourth is held out from the loop and used only for measurement/reporting. Algorithm pseudocode selects S* on development TSR/AvgScore and evaluates T_eval only for reporting.

simulator_agent_side_metrics_percent.external_similarity_validation: 200 evaluation-set simulated dialogues, two domain experts, blind comparison against real tickets across intent expression, information-reveal pace and emotion trajectory.

verified.model_assignment: Skill Editor/Generator uses deepseek-v4-pro. Verifier, User Agent, Attributor and Governor all use minimax-m3. Thus Generator != Evaluator is enforced, but simulator and verifier are not different model families.
verified.production_promotion: The paper explicitly states that no revision reaches production without human confirmation; the end-to-end architecture ends with human confirmation before production rollout.

scope_clarifications: Table 2's monotone Single-turn-QA and SkillEvo R1-R4 curves are not raw current-round successive versions: at each round, the reported version is the best version selected on the development set up to that round. The per-round values therefore include a best-so-far selection operator.

The held-out evaluation quarter is outside the algorithmic adaptation loop, but the paper reports evaluation-set TSR for every round. It is therefore a reusable reporting holdout, not a strictly one-shot final lockbox whose result is never inspected until the end.

The -7.1-point RegR change is an across-transition decline within the full SkillEvo sequence (28.2 -> 21.1), not a with-governance versus without-governance ablation. Direct governance evidence is stronger for TSR (81.8 vs 78.6) and bloat (2.8% vs 16.2%); the -7.1 figure alone does not identify governance's causal effect.

Dual-sided orthogonal evaluation separates simulator-side coverage/fidelity from agent-side accuracy by responsibility and denominator, but the User Agent and Verifier share minimax-m3. Do not describe this as independent-model simulator-versus-judge separation.

Human confirmation is a real production deployment gate outside the autonomous loop. It is distinct from experimental version selection: the algorithm selects checkpoints on development TSR/AvgScore, and once fact consistency holds it does not use a scalar TSR gate to accept each intermediate candidate.

No official public code repository was identified by the arXiv record or an exact-title GitHub repository search in this scoped verification. The paper supplies prompts, pseudocode, model assignments and hyperparameters, but explicitly withholds the production ticket dataset for privacy/commercial-confidentiality reasons.
material_conclusion: The worker's secondary-extraction numerical claims are primary-verified. The important corrections are that R1-R4 monotonicity includes best-so-far development-set selection, the 7.1-point regression reduction is not a governance ablation, simulator/verifier separation is metric-responsibility separation rather than model independence, and SkillEvo does have both an adaptation-external reporting holdout and a mandatory human production-confirmation gate. The holdout is reused for per-round reporting, so it should not be promoted to a one-shot untouched lockbox claim.
